references.why: Re-personed paraphrase of the verse; Segond reads 'il est réservé aux hommes de mourir une seule fois, après quoi vient le jugement'.
Re-personed ('our eyes' for Segond's 'leurs yeux').
Allusion re-personed in the first person; Segond 'comme n’en ayant pas'.
Bunyan omits 'narrow is the way', so Segond's plural agreement ('resserré le chemin qui mènent … qui les trouvent') cannot stand; Segond wording kept otherwise.
Re-personed into the third person ('his disciple'); Segond's list kept.
Re-cast as a direct address ('ye cannot be justified'); Segond 'ce n’est pas par les œuvres de la loi que l’homme est justifié'.
Re-personed from Segond's plural ('que vous ne périssiez dans votre voie') to the singular addressed to Christian; the second half is Segond verbatim.
Re-personed into the third person plural (Segond: « je ne mettrai pas dehors celui qui vient à moi »).
Bunyan applies the verse's two adjectives (strait, narrow) to the way itself; Segond's « étroite est la porte, resserré le chemin » is restructured.
Segond's wording, turned from indirect speech into direct (drops « souviens-toi que … que »), not a contiguous substring.
Re-personed into the first person by the man in the cage; keeps Segond's « pour leur part ».
Re-personed into the first person; Segond's words « tenu pour profane le sang » and « outragé l’Esprit de la grâce ».
Uncited quotation, re-personed (« which shall devour me as an adversary »); follows Segond's « l’ardeur d’un feu qui dévorera les rebelles ».

Blended paraphrase of Matt 13:30 (tares), Matt 3:12 (chaff), Mal 4:1 (stubble) and Rev 20 (burning lake). The source's marginal 'Matt. 18:30' is plainly wrong (that verse is about the unforgiving servant; the tares are 13:30) — kept as printed.
Re-personed as a command (Segond: « il amassera le blé dans son grenier »; cf. Matt 13:30 « amassez le blé dans mon grenier »).

Bunyan's margin cites Mark 4:40, but these words are not in that verse (Segond: « Pourquoi avez-vous ainsi peur? Comment n’avez-vous point de foi? »); they echo Proverbs 24:10 (KJV 'thy strength is small'). Reference kept as in the source; words rendered from Bunyan.

Bunyan follows the KJV margin 'persuade' (Segond: « Que Dieu étende les possessions de Japhet, qu’il habite dans les tentes de Sem ») and recasts the wish as a relative clause, so the verse is re-phrased around his reading.
Re-personed into Christian's first person; follows Segond's wording otherwise.
Re-personed (first person) and 'pays' made explicit (masculine), so Segond's 'une meilleure, c’est-à-dire une céleste' cannot stand verbatim.
Bunyan paraphrases ('that which is best / that which is worst'); keeps Segond's 'est attaché à moi' frame.
Re-personed from Segond's 'aux yeux de ses gendres, il parut plaisanter'.
Past tense ('thou hast delivered') and Bunyan's added 'from their blood'; Segond has 'tu sauveras ton âme'.
Re-personed (third person) from Segond's 'Au jour où je me lèverai pour le butin'.
Segond's words, but its feminine forms (Zion speaking: « mon ennemie », « tombée ») put in the masculine for Christian
Segond's wording with its repeated « Dans » dropped, so it reads as Bunyan's nominal description, and cut by his interjection « (sinon un Chrétien) »
Uncited echo of KJV Ps 71:16 ("I will go in the strength of the Lord GOD"); Segond reads « Je dirai tes œuvres puissantes, Seigneur Éternel! », which lacks the words Christian's cry depends on
Segond has « Il change les ténèbres en aurore »; Bunyan's point is the shadow of death (the valley's name) turned to morning, so « l’ombre de la mort » kept
Segond is a past-tense lament (« Quand sa lampe brillait sur ma tête, Et que sa lumière me guidait dans les ténèbres! »); Bunyan applies it in the present, and « go through darkness » is the point
Bunyan applies the verse to Wanton ('shall fall into HER pit'); Segond's 'y tombera' refers back to 'la bouche des étrangères', so the pit is re-attached to her.

Uncited; Bunyan gives the verse as an imperative ('Put off the old man with his deeds'), Segond has a participle ('vous étant dépouillés du vieil homme et de ses œuvres'); 'vieil homme' kept for the pun on the aged Adam.

Uncited allusion (KJV Ps 34:6); re-personed to first person and past tense ('he heard me, and delivered me out of all my troubles'); Segond: 'l’Éternel entend, Et il le sauve de toutes ses détresses'.

Uncited allusion to KJV 'valiant for the truth upon the earth'; Segond reads 'Ce n’est pas par la vérité qu’ils sont puissants dans le pays', which loses 'valiant for truth' (the phrase later names Vaillant-pour-la-Vérité).
Allusion in the song ('quit themselves like men', KJV); fitted to the verse line; Segond: 'soyez des hommes'.
Re-personed paraphrase of Paul's 'though I have all knowledge… I am nothing' into the third person.
Bunyan blends Matthew 13:51 with John 13:12-17 and his argument turns on 'know'; Segond's 'Avez-vous compris' would lose the knowing/doing contrast.
Bunyan condenses the verse; Segond's 'ayant connu… n’a rien préparé et n’a pas agi selon sa volonté' does not carry the same compact wording.
Segond's wording reshaped into Faithful's question about 'your religion' (inserted 'et non').
KJV 'From such withdraw thyself' (Textus Receptus); Segond's critical text omits the clause, so rendered here.
Re-personed to the plural 'you' addressed to both pilgrims (Segond: 'Retiens ce que tu as… ta couronne').
Bunyan re-persons it ('you must') and says 'kingdom of heaven' where Segond has 'royaume de Dieu'.
Re-personed from 'me' to 'you' (Segond: 'm’attendent').
Re-personed to the plural and 'I will give thee' changed to 'the King will give you' by Bunyan.
Re-personed as an imperative to 'you' (Segond: 'que ceux qui souffrent… remettent leurs âmes').

Source citation is wrong: the words 'must needs go out of the world' are from 1 Corinthians 5:10, not 4:10. Reference kept as printed; words rendered after Segond 1 Co 5:10 ('il vous faudrait sortir du monde') and re-personed.
The pilgrims turn 'Buy the truth' into a first-person statement; Segond has 'Acquiers la vérité'.
Participial adaptation of Segond 'Ne rendez point… injure pour injure; bénissez, au contraire' to fit the narrative sentence.
Juror echoes the mob's cry; Segond 'Ote de la terre un pareil homme!' put in the plural addressed to the other jurors.
Segond’s singular « juste à l’excès » put in the plural to fit Save-all’s ‘some that are righteous overmuch’.
Hold-the-world cites the KJV reading ‘lay up gold as dust’ in indirect speech; Segond (« Jette l’or dans la poussière ») would destroy his (twisted) argument.
Bunyan’s paraphrase of the verse, not its wording.
Segond has « contre l’Éternel »; Bunyan's argument turns on 'before the Lord, that is, in his eyesight', so « devant » is kept.
Re-personed (the people → the pilgrims) and follows KJV 'much discouraged because of the way'; Segond has « Le peuple s’impatienta en route ».
Opens with Segond's words, but Bunyan (KJV) has 'rather than life' where Segond reads « plutôt que ces os ».
Re-personed paraphrase (third person, past) of Segond's « donne sa vie pour ses brebis »; cited with 10:15.
Indirect (infinitive) adaptation of Segond's « N’oubliez pas l’hospitalité », embedded in the shepherds' charge.
Segond ends 'il dit de chacun: Voilà un fou!'; Bunyan (KJV) has the fool proclaim his OWN folly to everyone, which is his point about Ignorance. First two clauses are Segond verbatim.
Hopeful's verse paraphrase of Isa 27:11 (no understanding / he that made them will not save them), rendered as rhymed French verse.
Paraphrase of the verse ('in her occasion who can turn her away'); Segond's question 'Qui l’empêchera de satisfaire son désir?' recast as a statement.
Allusion re-shaped by Bunyan ('his voice is as the roaring of a lion'); Segond has 'rôde comme un lion rugissant'.
Segond frames it as God's question ('Est-ce toi qui ... revêts son cou d’une crinière flottante?'); Bunyan quotes it as a statement. Segond's words kept, recast.
First clause recast from Segond's question ('Le fais-tu bondir comme la sauterelle?') into Bunyan's statement; second clause is Segond verbatim.
Re-personed (we/us) from Segond 'Je ne crains pas les myriades de peuples Qui m’assiègent de toutes parts'.
Bunyan blends Job 9:13 ('the proud helpers') with Isa 10:4 ('fall under the slain'); Segond Isa 10:4 has 'tomberont parmi les morts'.
Segond reads 'la voie des violents'; Hopeful's argument turns on 'the paths of the destroyer' (echoing his own preceding sentence), so the KJV sense is kept for that word.
Segond 'nous marchons par la foi'; recast into Hopeful's question (infinitive).
Unreferenced echo ('believe to the saving of the soul'), re-personed from Segond 'ont la foi pour sauver leur âme'.
SOURCE CITATION WRONG: 'no lie is of the truth' is 1 John 2:21 (1 John 5:21 is 'keep yourselves from idols'). Reference kept as printed; words are Segond 1 John 2:21 verbatim.
Bunyan contrasts bodily eyes with the eyes of the understanding (KJV); Segond reads « les yeux de votre cœur ».
Bunyan re-words 'delivered for our offences' as 'died for our sins'; Segond « a été livré pour nos offenses » does not carry his wording.
Re-personed paraphrase; Bunyan's 'washed' (KJV) where Segond reads « délivrés ».
Re-personed: 'between God and us' where Segond reads « entre Dieu et les hommes ».
Re-personed: 'for us' where Segond reads « en leur faveur ».
Bunyan generalises Gen 6:5 into the present ('every imagination of the heart of man is only evil'); Segond is past tense about 'leur cœur'.
Uncited KJV-based allusion; Segond 62:5 reads differently (« comme la fiancée fait la joie de son fiancé, Ainsi tu feras la joie de ton Dieu »), and Bunyan re-persons it to 'them'.
Condensed: Segond puts it as a question (« Que lui direz-vous?… Que je suis malade d’amour »); Bunyan uses the KJV imperative 'tell him'.

Bunyan's point (the sleepers talk) rests on the KJV 'causing the lips of those that are asleep to speak'; Segond 7:10 has « glisse sur les lèvres de ceux qui s’endorment ». Cited Song 7:9 (KJV) = Segond 7:10.
Uncited KJV Ps 69:2 'I sink in deep mire… I am come into deep waters' (= Segond 69:3, which reads « J’enfonce dans la boue… »); Bunyan blends the two halves.
Uncited; re-personed (his for thy) from Segond « Toutes tes vagues et tous tes flots passent sur moi » (KJV 42:7 = Segond 42:8).
Uncited (KJV 'the sorrows of death compassed me', Ps 116:3 / 18:4); tense adapted from Segond's « m’avaient environné » to fit the speaker's present distress.
Condensed selection of 12:22 following Bunyan's KJV wording ('the innumerable company of angels'); Segond: « des myriades qui forment le chœur des anges ».
Uncited KJV wording ('each one walking in his uprightness'); Segond 57:2 reads « Il reposera sur sa couche, Celui qui aura suivi le droit chemin »; re-personed to the plural.
Re-personed (you for we) from Segond « nous le verrons tel qu’il est ».
Bunyan follows the KJV/Textus Receptus reading 'do his commandments'; Segond reads « lavent leurs robes ». The rest of the verse is mined (22:14b).
Re-personed to the plural (Bunyan: 'enter ye into the joy of your lord'); Segond « entre dans la joie de ton maître ».
Re-personed by Ignorance (I / the King / he) from Segond « Nous avons mangé et bu devant toi, et tu as enseigné dans nos rues ».
Re-personed from Segond's 'ils se reposent de leurs travaux' (third person singular about Christian).
Bunyan's paraphrase of 'they that sow in tears shall reap in joy', applied to Christian; Segond's wording kept where possible ('avec allégresse').

Re-personed: Segond reads "Ils se rassasient de l’abondance de ta maison"; here spoken of God in the third person ("his house"). Segond wording kept for "l’abondance de … maison". KJV Ps 36:8 = Segond 36:9.
Re-personed allusion; Segond has 'Dans la maison où je suis étranger', but Bunyan's word 'pilgrimage' carries the book's theme, so kept.
Allusion re-personed to the third person (Segond: « Recueille mes larmes dans ton outre »).
Segond verbatim except the poetic line-initial capital (« Moissonneront ») lowercased in running prose.
Segond verbatim except the poetic line-initial capital (« Revient ») lowercased in running prose.
Segond verbatim except the poetic line-initial capitals lowercased in running prose. KJV Jonah 2:7 = Segond 2:8.
Paraphrased allusion (Segond: « je prie ... pour ceux qui croiront en moi »).
Bunyan's paraphrase ('take the kingdom by storm') of the verse, not its wording.
Blended with Hosea 14:2 and re-personed; Segond words 'sacrifice de louange' kept.
KJV 'calves of my lips' re-personed; Segond's 'l’hommage de nos lèvres' adapted to the singular.
Segond verbatim except the poetic line-initial capital (« Je veux ») lowercased in running prose.
Re-personed by Bunyan (Christ speaking: 'I deliver them from the lions'); Segond: « Sauve-moi de la gueule du lion ».
Re-personed; Bunyan's 'my darling' read as the beloved pilgrim (Segond: « Ma vie contre le pouvoir des chiens »).
Re-personed to the second person (Segond: « Il fait tout à merveille »).
Re-personed KJV-shaped paraphrase ('He will be inquired of by them, to do it for them'); Segond words the verse differently ('je me laisserai fléchir... voici ce que je ferai pour eux').
Re-personed to Christiana (singular, 'found of him in peace, without spot, and blameless'); Segond is plural.
Bunyan quotes only the 'riches' half ('Give me not riches'); Segond's clause pairs poverty and riches ('Ne me donne ni pauvreté, ni richesse'), which would blur his point.
The Interpreter's lesson depends on the SPIDER (KJV); Segond reads 'Le lézard', so the subject is rendered from the English, the rest follows Segond.
Allusion blended with 'swallow down sin'; Segond reads 'L’homme qui boit l’iniquité comme l’eau'.
KJV-shaped ('thy latter end should greatly increase'), recast by Bunyan; Segond words the verse quite differently.
Re-personed from Segond's 'Notre cœur ne brûlait-il pas au-dedans de nous'.
Re-personed by Mercy (first person, future) from Segond 'tu as quitté ton père et ta mère et le pays de ta naissance'.
Re-personed (third person) paraphrase of Boaz's words; Segond's wording kept as far as the grammar allows.
Narrative allusion ('esteem each other better than themselves'), re-personed; Segond 'regarder les autres comme étant au-dessus de vous-mêmes'.
Unreferenced paraphrase of Luke 3:11 recast as a duty under the law ("give one"); Segond's 'partage avec' does not fit the argument's syntax.
Bunyan substitutes 'the King' for 'the LORD' (Segond: l’Éternel); otherwise Segond's wording.
Loose allusion, not the verse's words: Matthew 11:28 does not contain 'how sweet is rest to them that labor'; reference kept as given.

Bunyan's point (the punishment inflicted on the false tongue, as on the stage) needs the tongue addressed; Segond makes the tongue the subject (« Que te donne, que te rapporte Une langue trompeuse? »).
Christiana re-tenses and adapts Deborah's words to her own case; built on Segond's vocabulary.
Re-personed into Mercy's first person; Bunyan (KJV) has 'eternal life' where Segond reads 'la vie véritable'.
Echo of 'shall live for ever' recast by Mr. Skill as 'will make him live for ever'; Segond's 'il vivra éternellement' does not fit the grammar.
Adapted blessing: Reuben replaced by Mercy and 'his men' by 'her works'; Segond's second clause is also phrased positively ('soient nombreux').
Pluralized and altered: Bunyan substitutes 'godliness' and 'them that are grave and wise' for Paul's list and 'them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart'.
Bunyan expands the KJV 'the rain also filleth the pools'; Segond reads 'la pluie la couvre aussi de bénédictions', which drops the pools his image depends on.
Paraphrase re-personed to 'the King' and 'his' (KJV Hos 2:15 = Segond 2:17: 'je lui donnerai ses vignes').
Unreferenced allusion recast as an infinitive ('doing business in great waters'); Segond has 'travaillaient sur les grandes eaux'.
Unreferenced allusion re-personed to 'us' (KJV Jonah 2:6 = Segond 2:7: 'Les barres de la terre m’enfermaient pour toujours').
Bunyan recasts the verse in the plural ('them that walk… their God') and says 'the Lord'; Segond's singular wording and 'l’Éternel' adapted accordingly.
KJV idiom 'the root of the matter' (Job 19:28); Segond renders the verse quite differently ('la justice de ma cause'), so Bunyan's phrase is rendered literally.
Bunyan's loose paraphrase of the children's piping and mourning; the words are actually in 11:17 (11:16 introduces the parable). Reference kept as given.
Unreferenced; Bunyan says 'God' where Segond has 'l’Éternel' (La crainte de l’Éternel est le commencement de la sagesse); cf. Proverbs 9:10.
Re-personed (Segond: « Ils se repaissent des péchés de mon peuple »).
Unmarked allusion; Bunyan substitutes « the King of paradise » for « God » (Segond: « celui qui craint Dieu échappe à toutes ces choses »).
Bunyan adds « the heart » (Segond: « qui réjouit Dieu et les hommes »).
Re-personed to the boys (Segond: « afin que par lui vous croissiez »).
The pilgrim's name (Feeble-mind) hangs on KJV « the feebleminded »; Segond has « consolez ceux qui sont abattus ».
Segond reads « Au malheur le mépris!… » with no lamp; Feeble-mind’s own words just before (« comme d’une lampe méprisée ») depend on the KJV image, so the KJV sense is rendered.
Re-personed commission; Segond has « ceux qui sont abattus », but Great-heart’s point plays on « feeble-minded » = Faible-Esprit.
Re-personed allusion to Segond « ne discutez pas sur les opinions ».
Re-personed from Segond « Je me suis fait tout à tous ».
Re-personed (third person plural) from Segond « j’ai rendu mon visage semblable à un caillou »; no marginal reference in the source.
Bunyan re-persons the verse (us -> them); Segond's 'on nous fournit les choses dont nous avions besoin' recast in the third person.
Segond's wording recast into infinitives governed by 'qui savait'; 'avec douceur' keeps Bunyan's (KJV) 'gently', absent from Segond.
Segond 'il n’en manquera aucune' put into the subjunctive past and masculine (the children) to fit Bunyan's clause.
Bunyan re-applies the verse to 'this man' and the children (third person, plural 'them that are sick'); Segond's first-person feminine forms recast.
Allusion re-personed as narration (Segond: 'jeunes gens, parce que vous êtes forts').
Bunyan's conditional 'a little child might lead them'; Segond 'un petit enfant les conduira' recast.
Unreferenced; Bunyan re-persons the verse and substitutes 'innocence' for 'righteousness' and 'righteousness' for 'judgment'; Segond's frame kept.
Unreferenced quotation re-personed and turned affirmative (Segond: 'Vous n’avez pas encore résisté jusqu’au sang'); the words after 'tu as' are Segond's.
Unreferenced echo of 'la victoire ... c’est notre foi', re-personed to 'your' and applied to Valiant.
Unreferenced allusion re-personed into the narration (Segond: 'nous marchons par la foi et non par la vue').
Unreferenced allusion re-personed as an imperative to Standfast; Bunyan's 'when you have done all' (KJV 'having done all') differs from Segond's 'après avoir tout surmonté'.
Re-personed: Christiana addresses Valiant-for-truth with 'you' and substitutes 'my King will give' for Christ's 'I will give'; Segond wording otherwise.
Unreferenced allusion following the KJV 'hope to the end'; Segond reads 'ayez une entière espérance'.
Re-personed as the messenger's first-person token (KJV Eccl 12:6 = Segond 12:8); uses Segond's 'vase d’or' and 'cordon d’argent'.
Narrative adaptation of 'the grasshopper shall be a burden' (KJV Eccl 12:5 = Segond 12:7; Segond 'la sauterelle devient pesante').
KJV Eccl 12:4 = Segond 12:6; Segond's words ('s’affaiblissent toutes les filles du chant') recast as a standalone future-tense sentence.
Re-personed ('his pitcher'); KJV Eccl 12:6 = Segond 12:8, Segond 'que le seau se rompe sur la source'.
Bunyan follows the KJV 'O grave'; Segond has 'O mort' in both halves, and the two cries are distinct in the story.
Re-personed ('thy wheel'); KJV Eccl 12:6 = Segond 12:8, Segond 'que la roue se casse sur la citerne'.
Unreferenced allusion to 'the strong men shall bow themselves' (KJV 12:3 = Segond 12:5, 'les hommes forts se courbent'), made singular and personal.
